tasks.title: Add DNS Interception Infrastructure
tasks.description:
## Context
This task is part of the dns-in-firewall-errors change, which enhances sandbox firewall error messages to display domain names instead of just IP addresses. Currently, libsandbox.so intercepts connect() calls but the hostname has already been resolved to an IP, making debugging difficult. This section establishes the foundational data structures and helper functions needed to cache DNS lookups in thread-local storage with a 2-second TTL.

## Scope
- Add thread-local storage structure to hold DNS cache entries (hostname, IP, timestamp)
- Declare function pointers for real getaddrinfo() and gethostbyname() functions
- Implement helper function to store DNS lookups in thread-local cache
- Implement helper function to retrieve hostname by IP from thread-local cache

## OpenSpec checklist (reference)

- [ ] 1.1 Add thread-local storage structure for DNS cache (hostname, IP, timestamp)
- [ ] 1.2 Add function pointer declarations for real getaddrinfo() and gethostbyname()
- [ ] 1.3 Add helper function to store DNS lookup in thread-local cache
- [ ] 1.4 Add helper function to lookup hostname by IP from thread-local cache

The task list can be found at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md

## Implementation plan (suggested chunks)
1. Define thread-local storage structure with fields: hostname (256 bytes), IP (uint32_t), timestamp (time_t)
2. Add function pointer declarations for real_getaddrinfo and real_gethostbyname at file scope
3. Implement cache_dns_lookup(hostname, ip) helper that stores values and current timestamp in thread-local storage
4. Implement lookup_hostname_by_ip(ip) helper that checks cache validity (2-second TTL) and returns hostname or NULL
5. Ensure thread-local variables use __thread specifier for proper isolation

## Acceptance criteria
- Thread-local DNS cache structure defined with hostname, IP, and timestamp fields
- Function pointers declared for real getaddrinfo() and gethostbyname()
- Helper functions implemented for storing and retrieving DNS cache entries
- Cache TTL check validates entries are less than 2 seconds old
- Code compiles without errors in libsandbox.c
- All checklist items above are implemented and verified
- The task list at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md is updated (checklist items implemented are marked as done)

## Key references
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/design.md:L34-L43 (Decision 2: Thread-local storage with 1-2 second TTL)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/design.md:L45-L53 (Decision 3: Store single hostname per thread)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/design.md:L63-L64 (Risk: Memory usage for storing hostnames in thread-local storage)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L14-L30 (Requirement: Hostname-to-IP caching)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L32-L41 (Requirement: Cache TTL management)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L43-L54 (Requirement: Thread-local cache storage)

tasks.title: Implement getaddrinfo() Interception
tasks.description:
## Context
This task is part of the dns-in-firewall-errors change, which improves firewall debugging by showing domain names in error messages. getaddrinfo() is the modern POSIX DNS resolution function used by most programs. By intercepting this function via LD_PRELOAD, we can cache the hostname-to-IP mapping before the program calls connect(). This section implements the getaddrinfo() wrapper that captures DNS lookups.

## Scope
- Create getaddrinfo() wrapper function that intercepts DNS resolution
- Initialize real_getaddrinfo function pointer using dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)
- Call the real getaddrinfo() and propagate its return value
- Extract IPv4 addresses from successful resolution results
- Cache hostname and IPv4 address pairs with timestamp
- Ensure non-IPv4 results and failures pass through without caching

## OpenSpec checklist (reference)

- [ ] 2.1 Implement getaddrinfo() wrapper function
- [ ] 2.2 Initialize real_getaddrinfo function pointer using dlsym()
- [ ] 2.3 Call real getaddrinfo() and check return value
- [ ] 2.4 Extract IPv4 address from result if successful
- [ ] 2.5 Cache hostname and IPv4 address with current timestamp
- [ ] 2.6 Return result from real getaddrinfo()

The task list can be found at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md

## Implementation plan (suggested chunks)
1. Implement getaddrinfo() function signature matching standard: int getaddrinfo(const char *node, const char *service, const struct addrinfo *hints, struct addrinfo **res)
2. Initialize real_getaddrinfo using pthread_once pattern (similar to existing real_connect initialization)
3. Call real_getaddrinfo() and capture return value
4. If successful (ret == 0), iterate through result linked list to find AF_INET entries
5. For each IPv4 result, extract IP from struct sockaddr_in and call cache_dns_lookup(node, ip)
6. Return the original return value from real_getaddrinfo()

## Acceptance criteria
- getaddrinfo() wrapper function implemented in libsandbox.c
- Function pointer initialization uses dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "getaddrinfo")
- Real getaddrinfo() is called and return value propagated correctly
- IPv4 addresses extracted from ai_addr field of struct addrinfo
- Only successful IPv4 resolutions are cached (AF_INET check)
- Failed resolutions and non-IPv4 results pass through without caching
- Code compiles and links correctly
- All checklist items above are implemented and verified
- The task list at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md is updated (checklist items implemented are marked as done)

## Key references
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/design.md:L23-L32 (Decision 1: Intercept getaddrinfo() and gethostbyname())
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L3-L12 (Requirement: DNS function interception)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L17-L20 (Scenario: Cache successful IPv4 resolution)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L22-L25 (Scenario: Non-IPv4 resolutions pass through)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L27-L30 (Scenario: Failed DNS lookups not cached)

tasks.title: Implement gethostbyname() Interception
tasks.description:
## Context
This task is part of the dns-in-firewall-errors change to improve firewall debugging. While getaddrinfo() is the modern DNS function, gethostbyname() is still used by legacy applications. Intercepting both functions ensures broad compatibility. This section implements the gethostbyname() wrapper to cache DNS lookups from legacy code paths.

## Scope
- Create gethostbyname() wrapper function that intercepts legacy DNS resolution
- Initialize real_gethostbyname function pointer using dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)
- Call the real gethostbyname() and propagate its return value
- Extract IPv4 addresses from h_addr_list if resolution succeeds
- Cache hostname and IPv4 address pairs with timestamp
- Ensure failures pass through without caching

## OpenSpec checklist (reference)

- [ ] 3.1 Implement gethostbyname() wrapper function
- [ ] 3.2 Initialize real_gethostbyname function pointer using dlsym()
- [ ] 3.3 Call real gethostbyname() and check return value
- [ ] 3.4 Extract IPv4 address from h_addr_list if successful
- [ ] 3.5 Cache hostname and IPv4 address with current timestamp
- [ ] 3.6 Return result from real gethostbyname()

The task list can be found at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md

## Implementation plan (suggested chunks)
1. Implement gethostbyname() function signature: struct hostent *gethostbyname(const char *name)
2. Initialize real_gethostbyname using pthread_once pattern (similar to getaddrinfo)
3. Call real_gethostbyname() and capture return value (struct hostent *)
4. If successful (result != NULL && h_addrtype == AF_INET), extract first IP from h_addr_list
5. Convert network byte order address to host byte order and call cache_dns_lookup(name, ip)
6. Return the original struct hostent pointer from real_gethostbyname()

## Acceptance criteria
- gethostbyname() wrapper function implemented in libsandbox.c
- Function pointer initialization uses dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "gethostbyname")
- Real gethostbyname() is called and return value propagated correctly
- IPv4 addresses extracted from h_addr_list[0] field
- Address type check (h_addrtype == AF_INET) before caching
- Failed resolutions (NULL return) pass through without caching
- Code compiles and links correctly
- All checklist items above are implemented and verified
- The task list at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md is updated (checklist items implemented are marked as done)

## Key references
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/design.md:L23-L32 (Decision 1: Intercept getaddrinfo() and gethostbyname())
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L10-L12 (Scenario: gethostbyname interception)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L17-L20 (Scenario: Cache successful IPv4 resolution)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L27-L30 (Scenario: Failed DNS lookups not cached)

tasks.title: Update connect() Error Messages
tasks.description:
## Context
This task is part of the dns-in-firewall-errors change to improve firewall debugging. Now that DNS lookups are being cached, the existing connect() interception needs to be enhanced to look up hostnames from the cache and display them in error messages. This provides immediate feedback about which domain was blocked, allowing users to quickly update firewall allowlists.

## Scope
- Modify connect() function to look up hostname by IP before blocking
- Check if cached entry exists and is within the 2-second TTL
- Format error message with both hostname and IP when hostname is available
- Format error message with IP only when hostname is not available
- Ensure error message format matches spec requirements

## OpenSpec checklist (reference)

- [ ] 4.1 In connect() function, lookup hostname by IP before blocking
- [ ] 4.2 Check if cached entry exists and is within 2-second TTL
- [ ] 4.3 Format error message with hostname and IP if hostname available
- [ ] 4.4 Format error message with IP only if hostname not available
- [ ] 4.5 Update error message format to match spec requirements

The task list can be found at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md

## Implementation plan (suggested chunks)
1. In the existing connect() function, locate the section that handles blocked connections (where errno = ECONNREFUSED is set)
2. Before printing the error message, call lookup_hostname_by_ip(ip_addr) to get cached hostname
3. Check if hostname is returned (non-NULL) - this means cache hit within TTL
4. If hostname available: fprintf(stderr, "agentbox: Connection to %s (%s) blocked by sandbox firewall. This is not bypassable.\n", hostname, ip_str)
5. If hostname not available: fprintf(stderr, "agentbox: Connection to %s blocked by sandbox firewall. This is not bypassable.\n", ip_str)
6. Verify the error message format exactly matches the spec requirements

## Acceptance criteria
- connect() function modified to call lookup_hostname_by_ip() before blocking
- Cache TTL validation ensures only fresh entries (< 2 seconds) are used
- Error message with hostname follows format: "agentbox: Connection to <hostname> (<IP>) blocked by sandbox firewall. This is not bypassable."
- Error message without hostname follows format: "agentbox: Connection to <IP> blocked by sandbox firewall. This is not bypassable."
- Both error paths set errno to ECONNREFUSED and return -1
- Error messages printed to stderr
- Code compiles and links correctly
- All checklist items above are implemented and verified
- The task list at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md is updated (checklist items implemented are marked as done)

## Key references
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/proposal.md:L3 (Why: Makes debugging difficult because users must manually determine which domain was blocked)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/design.md:L1-L5 (Context: When a connection is blocked, it prints the destination IP address)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/sandbox-connect/spec.md:L6-L13 (Scenario: Connection to blocked IP with hostname)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/sandbox-connect/spec.md:L15-L22 (Scenario: Connection to blocked IP without hostname)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/sandbox-connect/spec.md:L36-L38 (Scenario: Error message with hostname)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/sandbox-connect/spec.md:L40-L42 (Scenario: Error message without hostname)
- internal/container/docker/libsandbox.c:L158-L164 (Existing connect() blocking code)

tasks.title: Testing
tasks.description:
## Context
This task is part of the dns-in-firewall-errors change to improve firewall debugging. Now that DNS interception and enhanced error messages are implemented, comprehensive testing is needed to verify the feature works correctly across various scenarios including cache hits, cache misses, TTL expiration, and multi-threaded operation. This ensures the feature is robust and doesn't introduce regressions.

## Scope
- Test DNS lookup followed by blocked connection shows hostname in error
- Test blocked connection without prior DNS lookup shows IP only
- Test cache TTL expiration after 2+ seconds between DNS and connect
- Test multi-threaded DNS lookups maintain thread-local isolation
- Verify all existing tests still pass with new interception code

## OpenSpec checklist (reference)

- [ ] 5.1 Add test case for DNS lookup followed by blocked connection with hostname display
- [ ] 5.2 Add test case for blocked connection without prior DNS lookup (IP only)
- [ ] 5.3 Add test case for cache TTL expiration (2+ seconds between DNS and connect)
- [ ] 5.4 Add test case for multiple threads performing independent DNS lookups
- [ ] 5.5 Verify existing tests still pass with new interception code

The task list can be found at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md

## Implementation plan (suggested chunks)
1. Add test in libsandbox_test.go that calls getaddrinfo() for a hostname, then immediately attempts connect() to the resolved IP (which should be blocked). Verify error message contains both hostname and IP.
2. Add test that calls connect() directly to an IP without any prior DNS lookup. Verify error message contains only the IP address.
3. Add test that calls getaddrinfo(), sleeps for 3 seconds, then attempts connect(). Verify error message shows IP only (cache expired).
4. Add test that spawns multiple goroutines, each performing independent getaddrinfo() and connect() calls. Verify thread-local isolation (each thread sees its own cached hostname).
5. Run full test suite with `go test ./internal/container/...` to ensure no regressions
6. Manually test by building agentbox, running a sandboxed command that triggers blocked connections, and verifying error messages

## Acceptance criteria
- Test case added for hostname display in blocked connection error (DNS → connect)
- Test case added for IP-only display when no prior DNS lookup occurred
- Test case added for cache TTL expiration (2+ second delay invalidates cache)
- Test case added for multi-threaded operation with thread-local cache isolation
- All existing tests pass without modification (no regressions)
- New tests pass consistently
- Manual verification shows correct error messages in real sandbox environment
- All checklist items above are implemented and verified
- The task list at openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/tasks.md is updated (checklist items implemented are marked as done)

## Key references
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L35-L37 (Scenario: Cache entry within TTL)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L39-L41 (Scenario: Cache entry expired)
- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L46-L49 (Scenario: Thread-isolated cache)

- openspec/changes/dns-in-firewall-errors/specs/dns-caching/spec.md:L63-L65 (Scenario: IP not in cache)
